summary: Voters reject a town and a school budget at two referendums with low turnout, and the charter gives the final say to the council.
realLife: A town's voters rejected its general and school budgets in April, then rejected a slightly higher revised package in May, with turnout near six percent. Advisory answers split on the town budget, while most school no-voters said spending was too low. The charter allows two referendums, so the finance board and council would finish the plan, as they did the year before.
sources: Patch (Berlin, Connecticut), 'Deja vu: Berlin voters reject town, school budgets, now town officials', May 27, 2026: https://patch.com/connecticut/berlin/deja-vu-berlin-voters-reject-town-school-budgets-now-town-officials
